{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABjEn8yA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhMazTY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 417, "title": "Bring desktop Node support to parity with the Chrome extension, including AI models", "body": "## Problem

The standalone desktop application currently exposes only 7 of the Chrome extension's 29 built-in Node types. This restriction was appropriate for the initial Japanese dictation MVP (#401), but is no longer the desired product scope. The user explicitly requests that as many existing extension Nodes as possible, **including all feasible AI model Nodes**, be available and actually executable on desktop.

Current main: [b17ccf0](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/commit/b17ccf05688162d659becdf8bbe19cc5946178be).

- [desktop/graph.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/desktop/graph.js): hard-coded seven-Node subset; rejects subgraph bundles.
- [desktop/runtime.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/desktop/runtime.js): separate limited runtime factory and Japanese-only model cache.
- [desktop/management.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/desktop/management.js): single-model management UI.
- [desktop/main.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/desktop/main.js) and [scripts/build-desktop.py](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/scripts/build-desktop.py): asset request policy and packaging limited to the current Japanese ASR.
- [extension/graph.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph.js), [graph-runtime.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-runtime.js), [graph-model-preparation.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-model-preparation.js) and [model-cache.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/model-cache.js): existing production definitions, model/runtime construction and asset management that should be reused.

## Expected outcome

### 1. Actual desktop Node parity wherever applicable

The desktop Graph Editor and runtime should support the existing shared Node catalog by default, except for capabilities that genuinely depend on a browser extension host. Target all 28 currently applicable built-in types (all 29 extension types except ChromeTabAudio), not merely an expanded palette. In particular, implement the currently missing 21 applicable types:

| Category | Missing applicable Nodes |
| --- | --- |
| Sources / controls | Number, Button |
| Speech recognition | SpeechToTextMoonshineMediumEn |
| Translation | TranslateGemma4B, Plamo3Translate2B |
| AI text processing / condition | TextProcessingLfm2, TextProcessingQwen35, IfCondition |
| Speech synthesis | Supertonic3, Kokoro, Qwen3TtsStreaming, CosyVoice3Streaming |
| Processors | TextAccumulator, TextSlidingWindow, TextWindow, Hold, KeyedTextPair, KeyedTextCoalesce, KeyedPairedTextAccumulator |
| Outputs | SpeakerOutput, AudioOutput |

Preserve the seven working Nodes: MicrophoneAudio, SpeechToTextMoonshineSmallJa, Text, TextFormatter, Display, FloatingDisplay and FocusedInputTextOutputNode.

- All existing AI models are in scope, including CPU/WASM and WebGPU models. Do not defer them merely because they are larger, require asset management, or were excluded from the MVP. Electron provides a Chromium execution environment; reuse the production browser-compatible Workers, inference implementations, pinned model identities and settings wherever possible. Do not replace a model with a stub, a different model or a cloud service. A genuine hardware/runtime incompatibility must be detected and explained accurately, not disguised as a generic unsupported-node filter.
- ChromeTabAudio is specifically extension-host-dependent. Leave it unavailable on desktop unless the exact existing contract can be supported without requiring the browser extension. OS-wide/system audio capture and a new browser integration are outside this Issue. Do not silently reinterpret existing saved ChromeTabAudio nodes.
- Support the existing reusable Subgraph authoring, expansion and import/export bundle behavior on desktop, for applicable constituent Nodes. Reuse the existing subgraph implementation and constraints. Do not invent a second subgraph format.
- Make the graph palette, validation, runtime construction, model requirements and actual packaged resources consistent. No palette-only additions, dummy Nodes, or silent dropping of branches. Preserve shared typed ports, node IDs, settings, saved graph schema, explicit wiring and lifecycle semantics. Import compatible extension graphs without manual rewiring; report genuine host incompatibilities without destructive migration. Do not add a separate whitelist that unnecessarily keeps equivalent shared Nodes unavailable.

### 2. Share implementation, not running resources

Prefer reusing/refactoring the existing Node construction, preparation, cache, graph editor and common lifecycle code rather than maintaining two divergent implementations for the same Nodes. Keep only real host-specific boundaries (microphone permission/capture, browser-tab source, native focused text output, presentation/UI, storage and platform asset transport). Use the smallest coherent shared factory/helpers; no speculative plugin system, universal registry framework or unrelated rewrite.

- Desktop and extension remain independent applications with their own model files/cache, graph storage, workers, RAM/VRAM and sessions. Shared source does not imply shared running processes, external daemon, required browser installation or cross-app cache. Preserve the existing local-first/no-cloud behavior, narrow IPC, renderer sandbox and scoped model asset requests.
- Reuse the existing model catalog and graph-derived requirements, preparation/download progress, cancellation/retry, integrity verification, reuse, deletion/active-use guards, license/source notices and readiness/error presentation. Desktop Models must support the actual added models; Graph Editor/Live/Start should use the same coherent readiness semantics as the extension where applicable. Do not bundle model weights, download every model at launch, or load models unrelated to the selected graph. Preserve offline execution with prepared assets.
- Package all necessary existing Workers, WASM/JS runtime assets, manifests and license notices for supported models. Adapt the local protocol/CSP and exact asset request allowlist as required for the actual pinned files, without granting arbitrary network or native access. Ensure WebGPU initialization/capability detection works where supported by the packaged Electron environment; do not use unsafe GPU/sandbox bypasses to make tests pass. Clearly distinguish real unsupported GPU/device requirements from lack of implementation.
- Support existing Live functionality needed by the additional Nodes, including Button/Graph Actions, Hold, Display of structured items, playback/streaming Speaker and Audio player/WAV. A graph with a valid executable audio/action output must not be rejected just because it lacks the old Display-only requirement. Retain intentional host lifecycle/permission boundaries. Keep the current UI style and share existing UI components where practical.
- Preserve existing desktop dictation behavior (clipboard paste, current-focus delivery, Floating Display and generic TEXT routing); do not reintroduce focus locking, hidden filtering, or unnecessary restrictions. No redesign of the existing ASR, translation, LLM or TTS algorithms.

### 3. Scope and practical validation

macOS Apple Silicon remains the primary desktop build/validation environment; preserve the existing Linux X11 host and make shared Node support available there where the runtime permits it. Do not require all OS/GPU combinations to run every model. Use existing hardware/capability errors and document actual limitations. The goal is broad usable desktop parity, not merely research or a plan.

If a particular applicable Node truly cannot work with the existing Electron/runtime environment, investigate the concrete blocker, document evidence and track a linked follow-up for that specific missing capability. Do not use speculative incompatibility, large downloads, unavailable test permissions or optional real-device checks to arbitrarily drop the AI Nodes from scope. Clearly distinguish implemented, fixture-verified, real-model-verified and genuinely unsupported capabilities. Avoid holding the entire change for rare edge cases or hardware-specific validation that cannot run in the existing environment; normal review must still confirm actual implementation and representative automated coverage. If intermediate PRs are needed, use the repository's ordinary partial-work rules and do not falsely close the overall scope.

### Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Reconcile the complete extension Node catalog against desktop palette, validation, runtime and packaging; verify that every applicable type has a real implementation. List any concrete host-specific exceptions and why. No false parity claim. Support existing compatible graph/subgraph bundle round trips and representative execution; preserve existing saved graphs.
- [ ] Automated deterministic tests execute shared pure processing Nodes, representative control/action graphs, keyed history/Display, and desktop output paths. Verify graph composition, lifecycle, typed ports, explicit provisional/final wiring and snapshot isolation without duplicating the entire shared Node unit-test suite.
- [ ] Exercise each newly supported AI model's actual desktop construction, model requirement/manifest, worker/runtime loading and output boundary with existing fixtures or the lightest meaningful packaged integration checks. Exercise representative CPU/WASM and WebGPU real-model smoke paths where existing hardware/verified assets allow. Reuse upstream model validation; do not require exhaustive real inference across every model, language, voice, GPU and OS, or repeatedly download large weights for review iterations. Never report mocked inference as real. A model must not be presented as working if its runtime or package assets are known to be missing.
- [ ] Verify desktop multi-model preparation/progress/retry/cancel/cache reuse/deletion/active-use behavior, pinned integrity and offline-ready operation. Test model-specific capability errors and correct packaged asset request boundaries. Package remains weight-free; extension and desktop remain independently executable.
- [ ] Build and launch the macOS desktop package; run applicable focused desktop checks, `npm test`, affected extension/MV3 regressions and packaging checks, plus relevant existing Linux checks where available. Use the lightest appropriate validation layers per development-flow guidance. Native independent-app permission-dependent checks and unavailable hardware-specific/manual tests are optional, not a human approval/closure gate.
- [ ] Update README/desktop guide/PR with the actual supported Nodes, setup and model requirements, graph portability, tested environment, commands/results and remaining concrete limitations. Provide example graphs or concise setup steps for translation, text processing and TTS on desktop. Run `git diff --check`.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Optional real-device/user verification is not a closure condition. Track subsequently discovered defects separately.

## Context

Follow-up to #401 and parent product vision #7. The user explicitly wants desktop to support the browser extension's Nodes as broadly as possible, including AI inference, not just deterministic processors. Follow the [node design principles](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/README.md#design-principles), [local execution and platform direction](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/processing-pipeline.md#local-execution-and-platform-direction), [port contracts](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/port-contracts.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md).
